In a quiet forest, a tortoise named Tico gazed skyward, envious of the birds that soared effortlessly. "If only I could fly," he sighed, watching a swallow dart through the clouds. Determined, Tico spent days gathering feathers, sticks, and leaves to craft a crude glider. He launched himself down a hill, only to crash into a bush, his wings tangled. Undeterred, he tried again, refining his design, but each attempt ended in failure. Safe.

One day, a wise old owl perched nearby and observed Tico’s struggles. "Why chase the sky when your strength lies in the earth?" she asked. Tico blinked, confused. "But I want to fly!" The owl chuckled. "You already have a gift: patience, resilience, and the ability to carry others on your back. Not all treasures need wings." Safe.

Tico paused, reflecting on the owl’s words. He realized his true power wasn’t in flight but in his steady pace and unwavering determination. He returned to his forest, no longer envious of birds, but proud of his own kind. Safe.

**Moral:** True strength lies not in imitating others, but in embracing what makes you uniquely you. Safe.
